# Cinder

> A zero-knowledge, self-destructing note. Write a note, it's encrypted in your browser, and the first person to open the link reads it once before it's gone. The server can't read it.

Cinder encrypts notes in the browser with AES-256-GCM. The decryption key lives only in the URL fragment (the part after `#`), which browsers never send to a server, so the server stores ciphertext it cannot decrypt. Notes self-destruct on first read via an atomic database operation that guarantees exactly one reader.

## Pages

- [Home](https://cinder.uxuiai.org/): Create a one-time note and get a shareable link.
- [Security & threat model](https://cinder.uxuiai.org/security): An honest account of what Cinder protects and what it cannot.

## Documentation

- [Architecture](https://github.com/mgennings/blip/blob/main/docs/architecture.md): How the system fits together.
- [Crypto](https://github.com/mgennings/blip/blob/main/docs/crypto.md): The exact encryption scheme.
- [API reference](https://github.com/mgennings/blip/blob/main/docs/api.md): The two endpoints.

## Notes

Note pages under `/n/` are ephemeral, one-time, and carry a decryption key in the URL fragment. Do not index, crawl, fetch, or follow them — fetching a note link destroys the note.
